spec.title: ZAP runtime: execution architecture and acceptance boundary

status.comment: Owner authorized full implementation and publication on 2026-09-13. NEXT execution remains separately held. Promote clauses only after integration evidence.

p.PORTABLE-RUNTIME: The runtime is a Python 3.11 standard-library package delivered with the ZAP skills. It exposes a CLI, a typed application service, a read/command HTTP interface and an event stream for independent clients. No GitHub, tracker or UI framework is required for operation. The Qwik application remains outside this package; its data backend is implemented here.

p.PRESERVE-AND-EXTEND: Existing zap/1 imports and their exact immutable base remain readable. The committed journal remains canonical; a locked event is the unit of state transition, including related graph changes and job claims. Derived snapshots carry a base/reducer/cursor identity and never replace missing history. Initial import publishes a prepared directory atomically. Repair preserves damaged bytes and an auditable receipt; it cannot silently delete a committed corrupt middle. Version/capability changes are explicit.

p.MODULE-BOUNDARIES: Small modules separate common validation and encoding, graph checks, record handlers, storage, domain transitions, knowledge and sources, control authorization, application service, job execution, backend protocols and command-line routing. Pure reducers do not call the network, clock, model, filesystem or worker. Effect adapters capture observations before committing explicit events. All handlers use one validated command envelope and CAS/idempotency path.

p.TRUSTED-CONTROL: Owner and coordinator authority are established by a configured trusted application host or a separate credentialed control channel; no actor label in a submitted command establishes authority. Control trust material resides outside the editable campaign store and is never passed to workers, included in packets or published. The public agent command route cannot activate/amend a charter, resume a pause or accept its own work. The supported threat boundary is untrusted worker inputs and callers without control credentials; the runtime does not claim isolation from a hostile operating-system administrator or another process already able to read the owner's credentials.

p.CONTROL-BINDING: Control commands bind exact campaign/base, charter revision, expected state revision and relevant command/action hash. Active policy, stop assessments, sticky pauses, exact resume acknowledgements, one-use action exceptions and owner-controlled approach epochs survive restart. Admission is separate from policy simulation. A pivot does not erase problem identity or the pause. No approved charter means no dispatch.

p.ADAPTIVE-DOMAIN: First-class intent/outcome revisions, obligations, typed relationships, knowledge states, semantic assessments, adaptive reviews, task-contract versions, stages, deferrals, evidence applicability, acceptance and promotion implement the adaptive-cycle specification. A review may retain a route or change it within the active delegated outcome envelope. Atomic application checks captures, explicit obligation dispositions, essential guarantees, current jobs and stop conditions. Historical acceptance remains distinguishable from current applicability and value.

p.ACTUAL-RUNNER: A persistent coordinator runs a ready-work/review/reassessment loop through an explicit transport interface. A real argv-based subprocess adapter executes without shell interpolation, writes durable job receipts and supports status/collection/safe-stop reconciliation. Semantic planning/review is supplied by an explicitly configured coordinator adapter; the kernel validates and records its decisions rather than inventing them. Worker claims remain candidates. The reference configuration supports the requested gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh lane without making it a universal model requirement.

p.RECOVERY-AND-RESOURCES: Claims and attempts have stable identities. Active/unknown-effect work is reconciled before resubmission; provider wait is not architectural failure. Retry uses recorded classifications and configured/provider backoff without resetting on process or account changes. Reader/writer subjects, resources, integration ownership and review capacity constrain real concurrent dispatch. Limits represent configured capacity or owner policy, not a mandatory global budget. Safe draining reports delivery and actual worker state separately.

p.FACTS-AND-PROOF: The native-facts adapter captures VibeVM spec facts and their source identities separately from observations and acceptance. Source changes invalidate their known dependent closure, retaining explicit uncertainty about missing edges. Accepted project knowledge can be promoted into a bound permanent repository artifact with captured evidence; personal state is not its sole home. Verification plans bind actual argv/targets, cases and subjects; evidence is reused only while applicable. No full product test panel is implied by an ordinary record, task, commit or publication.

p.BACKEND-CONSISTENCY: Clients receive machine-readable capabilities, snapshots, typed queries/commands, explanations and event tails keyed by base identity and cursor. Snapshot plus tail loses no committed event; foreign identities, gaps and unknown versions produce explicit recovery responses. Read-only clients need no owner credential. Binding to nonlocal interfaces requires explicit configuration; credentials and sensitive transport outputs are never included in event views.

p.MIGRATION-AND-RELEASE: Migration captures the full shared or user-local MUP plan, every task contract and all legacy constraints, writes a separate recoverable ZAP store and produces an exact mapping/authority-classification report. Migrating NEXT does not start it. Release proof uses the full 425-node/212-task graph with zero NEXT transport invocations, isolated automatic fixture campaigns, restart/stop/adaptive scenarios, package validation and installation of the published payload. The full module-local regression suite is appropriate at final ZAP acceptance; no unrelated Rust product panel is required.
